The volume of the right circular cylinder described is \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"45 pi\">\x3C/span> and its height is 5. If the radius is \x3Cspan>r\x3C/span>, it follows that \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"45 pi equals, pi times, r, squared, times 5\">\x3C/span>. Dividing both sides of this equation by \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"5 pi \">\x3C/span> yields \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"9 equals r squared\">\x3C/span>. Taking the square root of both sides yields \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"r equals 3\">\x3C/span> or \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"r equals negative 3\">\x3C/span>.
